exercise.name: Incline Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Press
library_steps: Lie on an incline bench with dumbbells at your chest, palms facing in.
Press them up until your arms are straight.
Lower them slowly back to your chest.
exercise.one_line_summary: 30 deg incline bench, palms facing each other, elbows about 45 deg from the body at the bottom with forearms vertical; press to near-straight arms over the upper chest. Chest (upper part most) is the target; front delts and triceps help.

setup.why: Upper (clavicular) pec activity peaked at 30 deg; front delt took over at 45-60 deg.

setup.target: Hips on the seat, back and head on the pad, feet flat and wide on the floor.
setup.why: Study kept head and thoracic back on the bench.

setup.target: Neutral: palms face each other, thumbs toward the head, handles horizontal.
setup.tolerance: handle within 15 deg of the body's long axis
setup.why: Defines the exercise; a neutral grip kept clavicular pec activity at least as high as a prone grip.

movement.measure: upper arm angle from the torso side line
movement.end: 118 deg (arm vertical in the room, over the upper chest)

movement.measure: 0 = side, +90 = out of the chest, negative = below the torso line

muscles.emg: Clavicular pec ~30% MVIC at 30 deg, its highest of five angles (S1); neutral-grip seated press ~30% (S2).
Rises with incline; highest at 60 deg (S1). ~24% MVIC in S2.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Back pad near upright, press becomes a shoulder press.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Above 45 deg the front delt dominates (S1).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arms at 90 deg to the body at the bottom.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Loses the neutral-grip, elbows-in pattern the library describes.

sources.citation: Rodriguez-Ridao D, Antequera-Vique JA, Martin-Fuentes I, Muyor JM. 2020. Effect of five bench inclinations on the electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major, anterior deltoid, and triceps brachii during the bench press exercise. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(19):7339.
sources.what_it_gave: 0/15/30/45/60 deg at 60% 1RM: clavicular pec peak at 30 deg (~30% MVIC); front delt highest at 45-60; triceps ~15% everywhere. Shoulders ~45 deg abducted when lowering.

sources.citation: Muyor JM, Rodriguez-Ridao D, Oliva-Lozano JM. 2023. Comparison of muscle activity between the horizontal bench press and the seated chest press exercises using several grips. J Hum Kinet 87:23-34.
sources.what_it_gave: Neutral grip: clavicular pec ~30% MVIC; front delt ~24% with no grip effect.

clip_check.check: End: arms vertical over upper chest, near straight
Back on pad, hips on seat
Palms face each other, hands on handles
Chest strongest red in both pictures
